summary: Charles B. Jones works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. Supervised by Paul Groner, he earned his PhD in History of Religions from the University of Virginia in 1996, later serving as an associate professor at Catholic University of America.

Charles Bally was a linguist who studied at the University of Berlin (circa 1886-1889) and under Ferdinand de Saussure (circa 1891-1894). He held a post at the University of Geneva from circa 1893 to 1939.

Charles Burnett is a scholar of history, archaeology, and philosophy who studied at the University of Cambridge. He held positions at the Warburg Institute, where he became a professor in 1999, the University of Sheffield, and the Institute for Advanced Study.

Charles Cutler Torrey, a scholar of religious studies, history, archaeology, and linguistics, studied under Theodor Nöldeke. He taught Semitic languages at Andover Theological Seminary (1892-1900) and was a professor at Yale University (1900-1932).

Charles D. Orzech, who works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology, completed his dissertation at the University of Chicago. He chaired the Religious Studies Department at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and was a Fellow at the National Humanities Center.
Charles DiSimone is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Munich in 2016 and held a post there attested in 2021.

Charles Duroiselle worked in Buddhist studies, archaeology, and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Rangoon (circa 1908-1919) and as Superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of Burma (1912-1940) and Archaeological Survey of India Burma Circle.

Charles Edmund Godakumbura worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology, completing his BA, PhD, and D.Litt. at the University of London. He taught at SOAS University of London and served as Commissioner of Archaeology for the Archaeological Survey of India (1956-1967).

Charles Eliot was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology who studied at Balliol College, Oxford. He served in the Foreign Office (circa 1886-1926) and was principal of the University of Hong Kong (circa 1912-1918).
Charles Elliott was an Indology scholar who served in the East India Company from circa 1795 to 1827. He later served as Treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society from circa 1837 to 1856.

Charles Gabriel Seligman, active in history and archaeology, studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital Medical School. He held the chair of Ethnology at the University of London and the London School of Economics from 1913 to 1934.

Charles Goodman works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan in 2002 under Allan Gibbard and held a post as associate professor at Binghamton University.

Charles H. Long, a religious studies scholar, earned his BD and PhD at the University of Chicago. He taught at the University of Chicago, UNC Chapel Hill, Duke, Syracuse, and UC Santa Barbara, where he was Professor of History of Religions.

Charles Hallisey, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Colgate, Harvard, UPenn, and the University of Chicago. He held academic posts at Loyola University Chicago, Harvard University, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, as well as teaching at Amherst College.

Charles Henry Tawney was an Indologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as Principal of Presidency College, Chennai, Principal of Benares Sanskrit College, and Librarian at the India Office Library from 1892 to 1903.

Charles Li is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of British Columbia, attested in 2020, and a post at the National Centre for Scientific Research, attested in 2023.

Charles Malamoud is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris. He held academic posts at the University of Lyon (circa 1965-1979) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études as Directeur d'Études (circa 1979-1999).
Charles Oman was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at New College from circa 1878 to 1883 and held a post at the University of Oxford from circa 1883 to 1946.

Charles Otto Blagden worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Dulwich College and Corpus Christi College, Oxford, and held a post at SOAS University of London from circa 1917 to 1935.

Charles Philip Brown was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the East India Company College and under traditional teachers. He served in the Indian Civil Service (circa 1817-1855) and as Telugu Professor at University College London (circa 1865-1879).
